E1.evidence: Reproducer and error log: "1. Publish a map using map_server. 2. Run rosbridge_websocket. 3. Start a JS app that listens to the created map topic." and "[rosbridge_websocket-1] [ERROR] [1682343826.795809774] [rosbridge_websocket]: Exception calling subscribe callback: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'" (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/856); maintainer PR 882 "Closes https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/856".

E2.evidence: The exception is raised inside rosbridge's own PNG-compression routine, which on the ROS 2 branch still used Python 2 string idioms: at 7bbe58ba (ros2 head on the report date) rosbridge_library/src/rosbridge_library/internal/pngcompression.py has `i = Image.frombytes("RGB", (int(width), int(height)), string)` and `buff = StringIO()` with a `str` argument. A commenter identifies the cause as a missing Python 3 port: "I got the same error and found that the ros2 branch needs to include a part of #460." (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/856#issuecomment-1571345660); PR 460 had "update[d] PNG compression code to use bytes wherever applicable" on the ROS 1 branch. The crash occurs for any correct client that requests PNG compression; the remaining defect fixed later (PR 1044: "`pngcompression.encode()` returns `bytes` object" / "`bytes` objects are not JSON serializable") is rosbridge's own encoder output consumed by rosbridge's own JSON serializer. No assumption between the client and rosbridge is violated.

E3.evidence: The subscribe operation fails, but the failure is internal to rosbridge's compression code rather than a mismatch between the two units.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "Exception calling subscribe callback: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'" and no map data delivered (issue 856); after PR 882 a JSON error remained: "Causes `TypeError: Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable` when requesting robot maps via rosbridge" (https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/pull/1044).

ineligible_reason: internal: rosbridge's ROS 2 PNG-compression routine (pngcompression.encode) still used Python 2 str/StringIO handling, so it raised a TypeError for every subscription that requested PNG compression (ros2djs's src/maps/OccupancyGridClient.js subscribes with `compression : 'png'`, https://github.com/RobotWebTools/ros2djs/blob/develop/src/maps/OccupancyGridClient.js), and after the first fix still returned bytes that rosbridge's own JSON serializer could not encode. The defect lies entirely inside rosbridge_library and would occur with any correct client requesting PNG compression.
notes: Fix history: PR 882 (merged into ros2 as 501a926cee2bedebf1417dc1aac9c876faf91b9b, 2023-10-26) switched encode/decode to bytes/BytesIO but left `encoded = standard_b64encode(buff.getvalue())` / `return encoded` returning bytes; a user then reported the map still failed ("i built from the repo and installed from apt and i get same errors", https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/856#issuecomment-2967706426), fixed by PR 1044 (ros2, fb157a07668233aca8e4784a2baea0afcef07f0a) and PR 1045 (humble, 1d82b2dfa361e908b63babe9dd7e16408ac6727f), both `return encoded.decode()` ("Robot map requests now work (confirmed locally)"). CMU-cabot commit 60bb5ab5 is a fork fix (unmerged PR 861) combining both changes. I also considered a rosbridge_library <-> Pillow reading (a Python 3 str passed to PIL.Image.frombytes, which needs bytes) but that is a Python-2-to-3 porting defect inside rosbridge's code, not a change in Pillow's interface. A separate error in the thread ("Unable to import msg class OccupencyGrid from package nav_msgs") came from the reporter's client asking for a misspelled type name ("I think it is a typo, OccupencyGrid != OccupancyGrid") and is a different composition. Reporter: ROS Humble, Ubuntu 22.04, "Library Version: latest".
